headline: RadNet's DeepHealth unit has publicised a modelled study in which adding an AI risk score to prostate MRI readings would have avoided 18.9% of biopsies.
score_reason: Modelled, retrospective result published on 26 Sep 2026 and promoted by the vendor with no new clearance or sales news; lowered by 1 from 5.
importance_line: Could eventually spare some men an invasive biopsy, but the result is modelled on a cohort with many confirmed cancers, no biopsies were withheld, and it is promoted by the company selling the software.
summary: Mugglehead Investment Magazine reports that, in a study published in European Radiology on 26 September 2026, using an AI score on unclear prostate MRI scans would have avoided 149 biopsies among 787 men while still catching 98.4% of significant cancers, according to RadNet's imaging-software unit DeepHealth. No biopsies were actually withheld, so the study cannot show that skipping them is safe, and for individual lesions the AI caught fewer cancers than radiologists (78.8% against 88.8%).
notes: Study from 26 Sep 2026; DeepHealth release 8 Oct 2026. Share-price and revenue details in the article are left out.
